name: tailcat
description: like netcat, but over Tailscale's data plane, without Tailscale's control plane
one_liner: A simple way to send data directly between two computers over Tailscale's private network, without needing Tailscale's full account and login system running on each machine.
buyer: An IT or network engineer at a company already using Tailscale who needs a lightweight way to pipe data — logs, backups, files — between two machines without installing a full VPN client stack on each.
business_use_cases: A sysadmin streams backups or logs between two servers over an encrypted private link without exposing a port to the public internet.
A DevOps consultant builds quick one-off secure file-transfer or debugging tunnels for clients during incident response.
An embedded or IoT team uses it as a lightweight component letting devices talk to a central server securely without the overhead of a full Tailscale client.

money_ideas.idea: Offer integration or consulting work that uses it as a component inside a client's larger secure-networking setup, since the tool itself isn't a standalone product

steal_this: Honestly, this is infrastructure glue, not a product you package and sell on its own — the real move is a consulting offer: 'secure point-to-point data pipes for your infra' sold to DevOps teams who already run Tailscale.
